message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on the current property auction.

The auction is for NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE. The current bid is $121. I have $726 cash and several properties with four houses. p1 has a dangerous dark blue monopoly with only $29 cash.

p4 has $763 cash and a fully built light blue monopoly. p3 is bankrupt. The mortgage value of North Carolina Avenue is $150. I will cap my bid near that amount so I can mortgage the property and recover the cash.

A $122 bid would net $28 profit after mortgaging. p4 likely wants this property to complete a two-green monopoly with Pennsylvania Avenue and trade leverage against p1.

A split green monopoly would prevent p4 from completing a full set without trading. I am calculating the rent on p1's dark blue properties to assess landing risk.

I calculated the rent on p1's dark blue properties. Park Place with three houses costs $1,100 and Boardwalk with four costs $1,700. Selling all twelve houses from my pink properties would return about $600 in cash. Combined with my current cash of $726, I could cover the lower rent but not the higher one. I would need to mortgage some of my pink properties to pay the full Boardwalk rent.

I checked the mortgage values for my pink properties. St. Charles Place mortgages for $70, States Avenue for $70, and Virginia Avenue for $80. Even with full liquidation of all houses and these mortgaged properties, I would have about $1,546 total. That is still short of the $1,700 Boardwalk rent with four houses. A $122 bid would leave me with roughly $1,424 in liquid assets, which is also insufficient to cover that rent.

I will bid $122, matching p4's pattern. If they push past my $150 cap, I will drop out.
